# m.stocks.quotes

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

National best bid and offer quotes of US-listed stocks, tick by tick.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.stocks.quotes(symbols, *, on_error=None)
```

- [Methods](README.md#query-methods): `blink()`, `append_only()`, `ring(capacity)`, `last_by(by='Symbol')`, `history(start, end=None)`
- Read from: REST, flat files, WebSocket

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows its rule under [shared arguments](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Stock tickers, or `dm.ALL` for every ticker. |
| [`on_error`](README.md#on_error) | What a bad symbol or row does in this call (`dm.ErrorPolicy`). |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description | Read from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The row's instrument, as Massive's ticker. From REST: the request's `stockTicker` parameter; flat files `ticker`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under."; WebSocket `sym`: "The ticker symbol for the given stock." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the New York date of `Timestamp`. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's event time. From REST and flat files `sip_timestamp`: "The nanosecond accuracy SIP Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the SIP received this quote from the exchange which produced it."; WebSocket `t`: "The SIP timestamp in Unix MS." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `BidPrice` | double | The bid price. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `BidSize` | double | The bid size. This represents the number of shares buyers are bidding for at the given bid price. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `AskPrice` | double | The ask price. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `AskSize` | double | The ask size. This represents the number of shares sellers are offering at the given ask price. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `BidExchange` | long | The bid exchange ID | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `AskExchange` | long | The ask exchange ID | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Conditions` | long[] | A list of condition codes. See Stocks Condition Codes (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/market-operations/condition-codes) for what each code means. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Indicators` | long[] | A list of indicator codes. See the Conditions and Indicators (https://massive.com/glossary/conditions-indicators) glossary for what each code means. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `ParticipantTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy Participant/Exchange Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the quote was actually generated at the exchange. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `SequenceNumber` | long | The sequence number represents the sequence in which quote events happened. These are increasing and unique per ticker symbol, but will not always be sequential (e.g., 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, 11). Values reset after each trading session/day. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Tape` | long | There are 3 tapes which define which exchange the ticker is listed on. These are integers in our objects which represent the letter of the alphabet. Eg: 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C. * Tape A is NYSE listed securities * Tape B is NYSE ARCA / NYSE American * Tape C is NASDAQ | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `TrfTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy TRF (Trade Reporting Facility) Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade reporting facility received this quote. | REST, flat files |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together share it. It isn't Massive's time, and later rows can carry earlier times. On `history()` rows, it's the download time. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
